design_point.fsw_l_pairing: L is fsw-COUPLED - pick the pair, not the pieces. 500 kHz -> 10 uH (dI 0.833 A, r 42 %, I_L,pk 2.42 A, P_U1 0.924 W). 400 kHz -> 15 uH (dI 0.694 A, r 35 %, I_L,pk 2.35 A, P_U1 0.854 W - 400 kHz is thermally BETTER). 400 kHz with 10 uH gives dI 1.042 A (52 %) and is wrong. I_Cin,rms is 0.90 A either way.
design_point.basis: requirements.md s3/s4 + answers A1-A4 (binding); fsw/L derived in power.md s3-s4

rails.vin: bench DC power supply, 18-30 V, 24 V nominal (requirements.md s3, STATED - not a battery, not mains-derived, not automotive)

consumers.basis: DC average input current = (10 W out + P_loss)/Vin. typ at 24 V nominal with the power.md s2 loss of 1.227 W; peak at the 18 V LOW-line corner with 1.174 W (low line draws the most current). At 30 V it falls to 0.376 A. This is a RESULT of the loss budget, not an independent estimate.

consumers.part: Cin -> VIN pin pulsed segment (the copper that must be sized)
consumers.basis: The HS switch chops the input, so the Cin->VIN copper carries rms = sqrt(D) x I_L,rms, not the DC average: 18 V -> sqrt(0.278) x 2.011 = 1.060 A; 24 V -> sqrt(0.208) x 2.013 = 0.918 A. Heating goes as rms^2, so sizing this segment on the 0.62 A average would under-size it by 1.7x. This is why power_constraints declares VIN at 1.1 A.

consumers.part: input ceramic bank, >= 9 uF effective at 24 V bias, X7R, >= 50 V
consumers.basis: I_Cin,rms = sqrt(D x (Iout^2 + dI^2/12) - (D x Iout)^2) at Iout = 2 A: 0.903 A at 18 V (D 0.278), 0.819 A at 24 V, 0.752 A at 30 V. Peaks at LOW line because sqrt(D(1-D)) rises toward D = 0.5, which this converter never reaches. Requirement: bank rated >= 1.0 A rms at 500 kHz.
Requirement Iq <= 1 mA switching; 18 mW at 30 V, inside the s2 budget. No shutdown state exists on this board (no EN control).

rails.notes: Pass-through net: screw terminal J1 + input ceramic bank, no series element. Mode excludes fuse, reverse-polarity FET, TVS and pi filter, so nothing else sits here. 0.03 W = 2 terminal poles at <= 5 mOhm plus the VIN copper at 1.06 A rms. No upstream inrush rule binds: buck-upstream-inrush-limit is bounded to source_kind in [usb, usb-pd, poe]; this is dc-input, and answer A2 (no live hot-plug, supply ramps from zero) removes the lead-inductance ringing case. Ceramic-only Cin is therefore safe HERE because of A2 - not in general. 100 nF HF ceramic at the VIN pin is mandatory and must be tagged role=reg_input in decoupling.json (check_decoupling errors reg_input_no_hf otherwise). All input MLCCs >= 50 V and X7R (board surface reaches 85-95 C; X5R's 85 C limit is exceeded).

rails.regulator: SYNCHRONOUS, integrated-FET, Vin abs-max >= 36 V (answer A1), fsw 500 kHz, fixed 5 V preferred; asynchronous+Schottky analysed and REJECTED - see power.md s2

consumers.part: EXTERNAL resistive bench load - the only consumer of this rail
consumers.basis: requirements.md s3 STATED: resistive load, up to 2 A at 5 V; 0 A floor recorded there as the conservative reading of 'up to 2 A'. A resistive load draws no surge beyond its steady value, so typ = peak = 2.0 A and no peak allowance is carried. There is NO on-board consumer to itemise (no MCU, no LED, no second rail - all excluded by the ultra-bare-bones mode), so the rail budget IS the stated 2 A. Design ceiling 2.0 x 1.3 = 2.6 A.

consumers.part: output ceramic bank, >= 20 uF effective at 5 V bias, X7R, >= 25 V
consumers.basis: Ripple rms into the output caps = dI/sqrt(12): dI = 0.792 A at 24 V and 0.833 A at 30 V with L = 10 uH / 500 kHz. Trivial thermally (< 1 mW at 3 mOhm ESR); listed because it is the second current this rail's copper carries.
I_L,rms = sqrt(Iout^2 + dI^2/12) = 2.014 A at the 30 V corner; peak instantaneous 2.42 A. Covered by the 2.6 A declaration.

dissipation_breakdown_w.at: Vin = 30 V, Iout = 2 A - the WORST corner (high line), 500 kHz, 10 uH

rails.notes: Single rail, fixed 5 V, no trim, no sequencing (buck-en-softstart-sequencing: single-rail boards rarely need it - stated as 'none' explicitly). Worst-case board loss is at HIGH line, not low: input current is only 0.38-0.62 A so input-side I^2R is negligible, while switching loss scales with Vin and the LS conduction time (1-D) rises from 0.72 to 0.83. Efficiency 89.5/89.1/88.6 % at 18/24/30 V and 2 A. Light-load/no-load: forced CCM costs 0.15-0.25 W at 0 A and keeps ripple at ~13 mV, so A3 holds across the whole 0-2 A range; PFM/burst typically gives 50-100 mVpp at 5 V and would VIOLATE A3 - see part_requirements.light_load. A preload resistor is NOT available as a fix (mode excludes conditioning the datasheet does not require).

consumers.part: common return for VIN and +5V (non-isolated, common ground in to out per requirements.md s1)
consumers.basis: Output return equals the load current, 2.0 A; the input return is smaller (0.62 A max). Declared at the same 2.6 A ceiling as +5V.

rails.notes: B.Cu pour, unbroken within 14.3 mm of U1 - it is simultaneously the return path, the reference plane for the switch node, and the board's radiator (see thermal_constraints). Single-sided assembly keeps the bottom clear of SMT, so nothing competes for it.

blocks.name: U1 24 V -> 5 V / 2 A synchronous buck

regulator.package: exposed-pad required; non-pad SOT-23-6 / SOIC-8 excluded outright at ~0.92 W
regulator.p_ic_ceiling_basis: P8 check_thermal on 2 layers gives 73.8 C/W at a saturated 645 mm^2 pour, so dt_c = 70 errors above 70/73.8 = 0.948 W. The physical ladder would allow ~1.1 W; the gate is the binding number.
regulator.current_class: 3 A-class part, NOT a marginal 2 A part. Typical 2 A-class parts at 36 V sit near Rds_LS 130 mOhm -> P_U1 1.19 W -> 88 C rise on 2 layers -> check_thermal errors, Tj ~138 C. Typical 3 A-class parts sit at Rds_LS 42-80 mOhm. A 2 A-class part is not disqualified, it FORCES 4 layers (1.19 W x 51.1 C/W = 61 C rise, Tj ~111 C).
regulator.selection_rule: rank on Rds_LS, NOT on Rds_HS + Rds_LS: at D = 0.167 the LS FET conducts 5x longer than the HS FET, so LS conduction is 3x the HS term (426 mW vs 142 mW at 30 V / 2 A).

inductor.isat_a_min_hot: 1.3 x the part's MAXIMUM HS current limit at 100 C (typically >= 4.5 A for a 2 A-class part) - NOT 1.3 x the 2.42 A peak; buck-inductor-selection

cin.dielectric: X7R minimum (X5R's 85 C limit is exceeded by the 85-95 C board)
cin.hf_cap: 100 nF at the VIN pin, role=reg_input in decoupling.json

cout.note: Must sit inside the chosen part's datasheet C/ESR window - internal compensation assumes it. External-compensation parts mean re-deriving the network, not copying the table row (buck-bst-fb-output-caps).

regulation.prefer: FIXED 5 V output variant - removes the divider tolerance term and two parts. Watch the FB trap: fixed family members tie FB straight to the output sense point; do NOT copy the adjustable variant's divider out of the shared datasheet figure.
regulation.if_adjustable: 0.5 % divider resistors, same family, TCR <= 100 ppm/C (divider sits on an 85-95 C board), FB reference <= +/-1.5 % over temperature, sense point AFTER the output caps.
regulation.if_cot_with_type3_injection: Add the +Vramp_pkpk/2 term: Vout = (1 + Rt/Rb) x (VREF + Vramp_pkpk/2), and solve the divider against the union of [VREF_min, VREF_max + Vramp_max/2] (cot-ripple-injection-raises-vout - worth +3 % on an LM5017, enough to blow 5.15 V on its own).
regulation.budget: Worst-case SUM with 1 % divider resistors is ~3.7 % and does NOT close against A3's +/-3 %; RSS gives 1.95 % and does.

light_load.requirement: A3 binds <= 50 mVpp ripple across the FULL 0-2 A load range, including no load.
accept_any_of: part with a MODE/FCCM pin strappable to CCM
PFM/PSM part whose datasheet shows <= 50 mVpp light-load output ripple at 5 V with a comparable Cout
light_load.reject: A preload resistor is NOT an available fix - the ultra-bare-bones mode excludes conditioning the datasheet does not require.
light_load.escalate: If no JLC-stocked 36 V-class candidate satisfies any of the three, raise it to the owner (relax A3 at light load, or admit a preload against the mode). Do not silently ship a burst-mode part.

enable_softstart.en: Check the part's OWN behaviour first - most parts in this class auto-start off an internal pull-up, so EN ties to VIN or floats and NO parts are added. No UVLO divider (mode-excluded, and a bench supply has no cable-droop motorboating case: 0.62 A over 2 m of lead is ~0.1 V).
enable_softstart.soft_start: Internal. Cout inrush = C x Vout/tss = 65 mA at 26 uF / 2 ms - invisible to the source, and A2 means the supply ramps from zero so there is no inrush event at all.

part_requirements.bst_cap: Integrated-FET parts need the BST-SW cap - required, not optional. 100 nF is the family default; confirm value and rating in the chosen datasheet (buck-bst-fb-output-caps).

scout_crosscheck.read: research/buck-regulator.json, arrived after s2-s7 were derived; changes no conclusion
scout_crosscheck.rank1_lmr33630addar: Correct SHAPE per s2: synchronous, 3 A-class, exposed-pad SOIC-8-EP, 38 V abs-max, internally compensated, 400 kHz. P3 must confirm Rds_LS <= 85 mOhm and t_on,min <= 130 ns off the datasheet (the scout's ~3.9x margin at 400 kHz implies ~107 ns, which clears). At 400 kHz use L = 15 uH and P_U1 falls to 0.854 W.
scout_crosscheck.ranks_2_3_4_are_async: AOZ1284PI / TPS54560B / TPS54360B are asynchronous and power.md s2 rejects that topology here with numbers. NOT drop-in fallbacks: re-run the loss budget (+0.42 W board), add a thermal entry for D1 (~0.77 W), and expect the layer decision to flip to 4.
scout_crosscheck.rank5_xl1509: Independently excluded by the s5 regulation budget: +/-4 % guaranteed accuracy alone exceeds A3's +/-3 %. The scout reached the same conclusion separately.

layout_notes: HOT LOOP (P6 placement group): Cin (HF 100 nF first, then bulk ceramics) - U1 VIN pin - U1 GND/PGND pin, on F.Cu, smallest enclosed area achievable. This is the loop that sets the ~37 mV of the 50 mV ripple budget that capacitance cannot buy back.

SW containment: short WIDE pour, 1.6-2.0 mm wide, <= 8 mm long, <= 40 mm^2 total, F.Cu only, never on an inner layer, never near a board edge or a screw terminal. IPC-2152 constrains WIDTH (1.52 mm at 2.6 A / dT 10); EMI constrains AREA - both hold with a short wide pour.

A4 probe pad: the single switch-node pad plus its ground pad must live INSIDE the existing SW pour, not on a spur, so it adds no area to the noisiest node. Its ground pad returns to the B.Cu GND pour directly beneath.
FB routing: short, away from SW and L1, sense point AFTER the output caps. Keep the divider (if any) at the FB pin.
Cout ground and Cin ground return to the GND pour at separate points near their own pins - do not share a single narrow neck (buck-cin-co-ground-separation).
B.Cu: unbroken GND pour, no split within 14.3 mm of U1. This is simultaneously the return path, the SW reference and the radiator; single-sided assembly reserves it.

Thermal via array under U1's exposed pad: >= 16 vias (target 20-25 counting a ring in the surrounding F.Cu GND island), 0.3 mm drill, 1.0-1.2 mm pitch. 0.3 mm so the barrel can FILL at reflow; larger drills wick solder out of the joint. On 2 layers this array IS the heat path (192 K/W per via through 1.6 mm; 16 -> 14.1 K/W, 25 -> 9.1 K/W) - 8 vias instead of 16 costs ~10 C of junction. Tent on the BOTTOM side; windowpane U1's paste aperture so the array does not float the part.
F.Cu GND island contiguous with U1's pad, >= 100 mm^2, not fragmented by the SW pour or the VIN routing.
L1 pads: >= 40 mm^2 of copper each (0.29 W on an 85-95 C board), and a GND void under the inductor body per buck-inductor-copper-and-gnd-void.
Zero layer transitions on VIN / SW / +5V by design (single-sided assembly, all three on F.Cu); GND is plane-fed through the stitching field.

check_thermal will NOT verify the via array at dt_c 70 / 0.92 W (it warns only when dt_c/power_w < 73.8 on 2 layers, and 76 > 73.8). The array is a P6/P7 requirement enforced by review - a clean check_thermal is not proof it exists.

conditions: synchronous rectification (async's 1.71 W board / 0.77 W diode does not fit on 2 layers at any size)
P_U1 <= 0.95 W at 30 V / 2 A, i.e. Rds_LS <= 85 mOhm, i.e. a 3 A-class part - the condition most likely to fail
outline >= ~1000 mm^2, e.g. 38 x 28 mm, with an unbroken B.Cu GND pour
>= 16 thermal vias under the exposed pad
escalate_to_4l_if: chosen part is 125 C rated (dt_c drops to 55 and neither the screen nor the ladder passes)
P_U1 > 0.95 W at 30 V / 2 A - a 2 A-class part at Rds_LS 130 mOhm gives 1.19 W and lands here
the honest outline falls below ~900 mm^2
layer_decision.live_trigger_warning: The screen passes 0.92 W by only 2 C (0.92 x 73.8 = 67.9 vs dt_c 70). The layer count FOLLOWS THE PART: P3 must re-run this arithmetic with the chosen part's real Rds_LS/Rds_HS before P5 fixes the stackup.
layer_decision.what_4l_actually_buys: NOT a lower R_ba - board-to-ambient is set by AREA and h, and the board is already near-isothermal at 2 layers (spreading length 26 mm vs a 12-19 mm half-dimension). It lowers the LOCAL junction-to-board path by ~11 K/W (0.30 mm prepreg to In1 vs 1.6 mm to B.Cu), worth ~11 C of Tj. Board AREA buys more: 875 -> 1200 mm^2 is worth ~10 C at the same power. The mode's 'smallest HONEST outline' therefore has a numeric floor here: honest means >= ~1000 mm^2, because the outline IS the radiator.

rejected.why: +0.42 W (+33 %) board dissipation at 30 V / 2 A and a second 0.77 W hot spot whose Tj lands ~126 C on an SMB against a 125 C rating, with reverse-leakage positive feedback. The low duty cycle is the worst case for a diode: it conducts 83 % of every cycle at 30 V.
(24-5) x 2 = 38 W. Arithmetic, not a choice.
~1-2 efficiency points for two FETs, a gate/sense network and area, at 10 W. buck-selection-ladder rung 3 is the escape hatch for corners with no stocked integrated part; 30 V / 2 A is not one.
1.58 W at 1.0 MHz and 1.93 W at 1.4 MHz vs 1.29 W at 500 kHz, and t_on(30 V) falls to 167/119 ns against a typical 100-130 ns min on-time.
DCR scales ~4 mOhm/uH at constant package size, so 15 uH adds ~93 mW of I^2R and removes only ~25 mW of core loss.
Conditioning the datasheet does not require - excluded by the ultra-bare-bones mode. The fix has to be part selection.
Not required: A2 removes the hot-plug ring, so there is no damping requirement and no source-side inrush rule. Ceramic-only Cin. (This is an A2-dependent conclusion, not a general one.)

model_limits.part_model: s2 numbers model a TYPICAL 36 V-class integrated 2 A sync buck, not a part. Every conclusion is expressed as a limit P3 must meet.
model_limits.switching_loss: +/-30 % (linear V/I crossover, symmetric edges, no reverse recovery)
model_limits.core_loss: +/-40 % (anchored at 80 mW / 0.833 App / 500 kHz, not a vendor curve)
model_limits.r_ba: +/-30 % (textbook flat-plate convection + radiation). Cross-checked against the repo check_thermal model: 73.8 C/W on 2L vs the ladder's ~70 C/W effective - the two agree.
model_limits.duty_cycle: D = Vout/Vin ideal used for ripple; real D is 5-8 % higher with drops, which relaxes the min-on-time margin (conservative as written).
model_limits.net_names: VIN / SW / +5V / GND are this fragment's proposal - P2 must reconcile power.json to the final netlist names before P5.
